summary: Lynchburg, Virginia pastor and televangelist Jerry Falwell preached segregation, founded Liberty University and the Moral Majority, and fused American evangelicals into a political bloc that fought abortion, feminism and gay rights from 1979 on.

evidence.note: Falwell's birth in 1933 and his Lynchburg, Virginia origins
founds Thomas Road Baptist Church in 1956 and starts his broadcast ministry
1958 sermon defending segregation and attacking Brown v. Board
segregation academies, IRS tax-exemption fights and Bob Jones University as the movement's root
Moral Majority formed in 1979 with Weyrich and Phillips; long segment on its campaigns
1980 voter drive and endorsement of Reagan
Falwell blames AIDS on gay men and opposes research funding
Hustler parody, the libel suit from 1983 and the Supreme Court loss; later friendship with Flynt
death by heart attack in May 2007
whole part turns to Jerry Falwell Jr. (born 1962) and his running of Liberty
Liberty's online program, recruiter pressure and federal aid revenue
September 2019 student protests and calls for investigation close the covered years

notes: Part 3 is entirely about Jerry Falwell Jr. and Liberty University through 2019, so covered_span runs to 2019 and both are secondary subjects. The father Carey Falwell's bootlegging and violence (1910s-1940s) gets several minutes in part 1 but is treated as family background; covered_span starts at Jerry's 1933 birth. Anti-feminism and ERA opposition are folded into religious-right-culture-war. Animal-cruelty is borderline: one vivid anecdote of the father killing a worker's cat.
